body: Can you provide SQL and the `_form` generated?

This is a real (small) example. See column `kontoartID` which moved up. ``` CREATE TABLE `kontoplan` ( `id` INT(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT, `mandantID` INT(11) NOT NULL, `ktoNr` VARCHAR(6) NULL DEFAULT NULL, `bezeichnung` VARCHAR(45) NULL DEFAULT NULL, `saldovortrag` TINYINT(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT '0', `abschlussID` INT(11) NULL DEFAULT NULL, `fremdkonto` TINYINT(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT '0', `kontoartID` INT(11) UNSIGNED NOT NULL, `autosplit` TINYINT(1) NULL DEFAULT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (`id`), ); ``` ``` php field($model, 'mandantID')->textInput() ?> field($model, 'ktoNr')->textInput(['maxlength' => 6]) ?> field($model, 'bezeichnung')->textInput(['maxlength' => 45]) ?> field($model, 'kontoartID')->textInput(['maxlength' => 11]) ?> field($model, 'saldovortrag')->textInput() ?> field($model, 'abschlussID')->textInput() ?> field($model, 'fremdkonto')->textInput() ?> field($model, 'autosplit')->textInput() ?>
isNewRecord ? Yii::t('app', 'Create') : Yii::t('app', 'Update'), ['class' => $model->isNewRecord ? 'btn btn-success' : 'btn btn-primary']) ?>
```

Below is the var_dump of attributes. 

Btw.: Shouldn't the attributes function be **static**?

```
array (size=9)
  0 => string 'id' (length=2)
  1 => string 'mandantID' (length=9)
  2 => string 'ktoNr' (length=5)
  3 => string 'bezeichnung' (length=11)
  4 => string 'saldovortrag' (length=12)
  5 => string 'abschlussID' (length=11)
  6 => string 'fremdkonto' (length=10)
  7 => string 'kontoartID' (length=10)
  8 => string 'autosplit' (length=9)
```

Actually I think the order has to do with the attributes of the Model, which are dynamic and are fetched via `$class->getProperties(\ReflectionProperty::IS_PUBLIC)` in base/Model.php attributes().
I could not find any documentation on how to get them in a specific order and I might be wrong about this beeing the cause, maybe a core devloper could argue further for/against this;)
@kmindi, the  model attributes() sequence is correct. All generated views are fine except the **_form** views. I assume that gii doesn't process columns in the original order.

Oh I see. The approach used in gii\generators\crud\default\views_form.php is different than in for example in gii\generators\crud\default\views\view.php. There it uses getColumnNames which falls back to attributes for non activeRecord models. Maybe this approach should be taken for _form.php as well.

I dont't know where exaclty the order gets messed up for the safeAttributes, but I think it is important to only generate fields for safe attributes, as not all existing attributes(columns in the schema) are always available for mass assignment (http://stuff.cebe.cc/yii2docs/yii-base-model.html#safeAttributes%28%29-detail).
can you try that change? I can't test it and there are no unit tests for gii I suppose.

@kmindi, the fix solves this issue. Thanks for your effort.

Be aware that the fix is not published yet. I've copied your changes manually into  the gii generator code.
@samdark can you review the change aswell, thanks
@kmindi looks OK to me. Can you create a pull request?
